title: If I May Touch But His Clothes

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jesus had just come back across the lake, and the people were waiting on the shore. A ruler of the synagogue named Jairus pushed through and fell down at his feet. His little girl was dying, and he begged Jesus to come lay his hands on her so she would live.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jesus went with him. And the crowd went too, pressing in from every side, so close you could hardly walk. Somewhere in that crowd was a woman nobody was looking at.

verses.text: And a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years,

verses.text: And had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse,

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Twelve years. That is as long as Jairus's baby girl had been alive. Twelve years of doctors and remedies, of hoping and being let down. Every coin she had, gone. And instead of getting better, she got worse. Somebody knows that kind of tired, the kind sleep does not fix.

verses.text: When she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment.

verses.text: For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.

segments.speaker: woman
segments.text: If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: She did not make an appointment. She did not get in line. She did not even call his name. She had heard about Jesus, and that was enough. She came up behind him in that crowd, quiet, and she reached.

verses.text: And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague.

verses.text: And Jesus, immediately knowing in himself that virtue had gone out of him, turned him about in the press, and said, Who touched my clothes?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Jesus, immediately knowing in himself that virtue had gone out of him, turned him about in the press, and said, Who touched my clothes?

verses.text: And his disciples said unto him, Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And his disciples said unto him,

segments.speaker: disciples
segments.text: Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?

verses.text: And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The disciples thought that was a strange question, with all those people pushing on him. But Jesus kept looking. A crowd pressing in is not the same as a hand reaching out in faith. He knew the difference.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: And she knew she had been found. She was afraid, and she was trembling. But she did not run.

verses.text: But the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.

verses.text: And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He could have let her slip away healed and nameless. But he called her daughter. He let her tell all the truth in front of everybody, while a worried father waited and a whole town watched. Then he sent her home in peace. That is the story, Church. Not only the healing. The being seen.

first_reader.note: Drafted and read by Claude in the landing session; no free-model draft (QA_NO_FREE_MODEL not needed).

pastor.note: Faithful to Mark 5:22-34 and 5:42; her healing stays hers in the text, no healing promise to the listener.

cultural.note: She is seen, named daughter, never pitied; 'Church' used sparingly.
